titleEn: One Line at a Time, a Little Louder!

pages.text: "Duri's birthday song, everyone together!" Teacher Bau clapped. On the long window table, one candle burned before careless Duri. Timid Lala covered their mouth with both hands.
That morning, Lala had put a leaf crown at Duri's place. Lala wanted to sing loudest too, but those shoulders hunched.
The song began. Everyone opened their mouths wide and sang. Lala's mouth stayed covered. Not a sound came out.
The song ended, and Duri blew out the candle. At the clapping, Lala covered both ears. Lala had not sung a word.
Teacher Bau sat beside Lala. "You do not have to sing everything at once. One line at a time, a little louder!" Duri hurried over and sat beside Lala too.
Lala lowered those hands a little and sang very softly, "Happy birthday to you..." Just loud enough for Duri. Duri's eyes sparkled wide. "I hear it! I hear it!"
This time they sang together, a little louder. Lala's hands lowered to their knees. "One line at a time, a little louder!" Duri kept the beat.
Teacher Bau lit the candle again. Everyone sang together. On the last line, Lala's voice was loudest. "Dear Duri!" Duri blew out the candle.
Lala had three singing rules. One, hands down! Two, one very quiet line! Three, one line a little louder! During story time the next day, Lala raised a hand first.
Duri hugged Lala. "Your song was best!" Singing one line at a time made it possible to finish. Smiling widely, Lala said, "One line at a time, a little louder!"
